topic.name: The Sum and Constant Multiple Rules for Definite Integrals

question.explanation:
Splitting up the integral into the sum of two integrals and evaluating each integral separately, we get

\begin{align} \int_{1}^{e} \left(\dfrac 1 x + 1\right)\, \textrm d x &= \int_{1}^{e} \dfrac 1 x\, \textrm d x + \int_{1}^{e} 1 \, \textrm d x \\[5pt] %&= \int_{0}^{1} x\, \textrm d x + \int_{1}^{4} x^{1/2} \, \textrm d x \\[5pt] &= \ln x \Bigg|_{1}^{e} + x \Bigg|_{1}^{e} \\[5pt] &= \left(\ln e - \ln 1 \right) + (e - 1) \\[5pt] &= 1 + e - 1\\[5pt] &= e \end{align}

example.title: Evaluating the Integral of the Sum of Two Functions Using the Sum Rule

question.explanation: Splitting up the difference and factoring out the constants, we have \begin{align*} \int_{-1}^{0} (3z - 1) \, \textrm d z &= 3\int_{-1}^{0} z \, \textrm d z - \int_{-1}^{0} \textrm d z \\[5pt] & = 3 \cdot \dfrac{1}{2}z^2 \, \Bigg|_{-1}^{0} - z \, \Bigg|_{-1}^{0} \\[5pt] & = \dfrac{3}{2}z^2 \, \Bigg|_{-1}^{0} - z \, \Bigg|_{-1}^{0} \\[5pt] & = \dfrac{3}{2} \left(0^2 - (-1)^2\right) - \left(0 - (-1)\right) \\[5pt] & = -\dfrac{3}{2} - 1\\[5pt] & = -\dfrac{5}{2}. \end{align*}

example.title: Evaluating the Integral of a Polynomial Function

question.explanation: We split the integral into the difference of two integrals and factor out the constants. We get \begin{align} \int_{1}^{e} \left( \dfrac{1}{2y} - y \right) \textrm{d}y & = \dfrac{1}{2} \int_{1}^{e} \dfrac{1}{y}\, \textrm{d}y - \int_{1}^{e} y \, \textrm{d}y \\[5pt] & = \dfrac{1}{2}\ln|y| \, \Bigg|_{1}^{e} - \dfrac{1}{2}y^2 \, \Bigg|_{1}^{e} \\[5pt] & = \dfrac{1}{2}\left(\ln{e} - \ln{1}\right) - \dfrac{1}{2}(e^2 - 1^2) \\[5pt] & = \dfrac{1}{2}\left(1 - 0\right) - \dfrac{1}{2}(e^2 - 1) \\[5pt] & = \dfrac{1}{2} - \dfrac{1}{2}e^2 + \dfrac{1}{2} \\[5pt] & = 1-\dfrac{e^2}{2}. \end{align}

example.title: Evaluating the Integral of a Sum of Two Functions

question.text: Evaluate the following integral. Do not round the answer.
question.explanation: Splitting up the integral into the difference of two integrals and evaluating each integral separately, we get \begin{align} \int_{1}^{4} \left(2\sqrt{x} - 3x^{2} \right) \textrm d x &= \int_{1}^{4} 2\sqrt{x} \,\textrm d x - \int_{1}^{4} 3x^{2} \, \textrm d x \\[5pt] &= 2 \cdot \dfrac{2}{3} x^{3/2} \, \Bigg|_{1}^{4} - x^{3} \, \Bigg|_{1}^{4} \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{4}{3} \left(4^{3/2} - 1^{3/2} \right) - \left(4^{3} - 1^{3} \right) \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{4}{3} (8 - 1) - (64 - 1) \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{28}{3} - 63 \\[5pt] &= \bbox[4pt,border: 1px solid lightgray]{-\dfrac{161}{3}}. \end{align}
